additional_info.subject: RE: ID0478737-DC/Si-D/-FR[Y2 / PD 312571675/24] Rear Busbar Heat Trace CRM:03097000465
additional_info.body:
Dear Thibaut,
Thank you for contacting our eMobility Support, I hope this email finds you well.
Following your request I could check the previous ticket and we have sent you an email with the following information on
12/4/2025.
At the end of the email we also have the following information:
• As there are no clear signs of arcing or electrical burnt areas, I would assume that the charger can still be operated for the moment.
---/
I am reaching out in regards of ticket
ID0464385
to provide you a summary from today's onsite activity and remote inspection of the charger.
As per my understanding. last week service colleagues from Engie went onsite for charger Y2 / PD 312571675/24, as the main fan was constantly spinning at 100% with very high humidity values detected by sensors.
The situation they found was a charger with all copper bars blackened, and filter mats completely impregnated with dust and mold (see photos attached).
Today I performed a complete remote inspection of the charger with a technician onsite:
All the copper bars—from AC input before MCCB, after MCCB, PE conductor, DC+ and DC- bars—are blackened, as if oxidized by humidity.
The copper bars on the roof look the same as well.
I inspected the charger carefully and found no clear sign of dust or particles.
I inspected all the visible junctions and connections of the copper bars, and I could not see any sign of electrical arcing, hot spots, or false contact.
There are signs of overheating in the AC power cables going from the copper bars to the power converters (see photos). I assume these cables suffered of overheating, as they are the lowest power cables in the charger, and ventilation was probably not enough provided enough.
Please proceed to replace these cables.
As per spare part manual, I report here the MLFB, but I would suggest to reach out to serviceability manager for more info on the components to be ordered:
Only one bar (see photo attached) has a worse aspect compared to the others, as if it is not oxidized but corroded.
The copper bars of the switching matrix are cleaner. In my eyes, it is clear that these copper bars were unmounted and mounted back, probably for TDK contactor replacement. On these bars, there are clear fingerprints and marks of human touch.
We tried to clean the copper bars with an isopropyl solution to ensure it was not dirt, dust, or coating.
As there are no clear signs of arcing or electrical burnt areas, I would assume that the charger can still be operated for the moment. I already reached out to QA department, to provide me with an assessment whether such oxidation of the bars might introduce some electrical safety risk, as well as the marks on the switching matrix bars, and what should be the way forward.
With best regards,
eMobility Technical Support Team – Felipe Moraes
Please do not change the subject line when replying to this email.
